purpose: Release floor for security-sensitive SAT runtime dependencies. Official packages fail closed when the policy is stale or a detected component is below its floor.

openssl.reason: SAT release packaging is pinned to the OpenSSL 3.5 LTS series. 3.5.9 (2026-09-29) fixes CVE-2026-84782 (High, CVSS 8.2, an out-of-bounds read in DTLS handshake retransmission) and twelve Low advisories; 3.5.8 fixed CVE-2026-14456 (QUIC server) and the 2026-08-25 advisories. SAT uses TLS over TCP only (HTTPS, libssh2), no DTLS, QUIC or TLS listener, but the floor is the fixed release. Windows builds it through ports/openssl, Linux through tools/Build-ThirdParty-Linux.sh. Reviewed 2026-10-27; the method is in the security findings under docs.
openssl.advisory: CVE-2026-84782 (High, DTLS), the 2026-09-29 advisories; CVE-2026-14456 and the 2026-08-25 advisories

libarchive.reason: 3.8.10 (2026-10-14) is the current security and bugfix release. SAT opens customers' archives, so archive parsing is its largest exposure. Windows builds it through ports/libarchive, Linux through tools/Build-ThirdParty-Linux.sh. Reviewed 2026-10-27.

libssh2.reason: CVE-2026-55200 (GHSA-r8mh-x5qv-7gg2, CVSS 8.1, AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H): out-of-bounds write in ssh2_transport_read() which fails to enforce upper bounds on the packet_length field. A malicious or compromised SSH server sends crafted packets with excessively large packet_length values to corrupt heap memory and achieve remote code execution on the connecting client; a public PoC exists. All releases up to and including 1.11.1 are affected. SAT is an SSH/SFTP client and completes a full key exchange inside ssh_probe_host_key() before any host-key fingerprint is computed, so SAT host-key trust provides no mitigation for this defect. The advisory names a FIX COMMIT, not a fixed release: 97acf3df ("transport.c: Additional boundary checks for packet length", 2026-06-12). Upstream has published no release since 1.11.1 (2024-10-16) and master declares itself 1.11.2_DEV, so the fix will ship as 1.11.2. The floor is therefore 1.11.2, and requiredFixCommit additionally forces any pre-release build to be provably built from that commit - a 1.11.2_DEV snapshot predating the fix reports the same version and must not pass.

sqlite.reason: Current reviewed SQLite maintenance floor for SAT's bundled database runtime.
